findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign the mcp compose service's REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID + REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY env vars, the opcert-ed25519-key secret mount, and its fetch-secrets.sh materialization to an explicit child (fd4a/esok and 9015/avians, or add to b173's scope) so b173's move-1 signing has an owner and add it as a b173 dependency.
evidence: b173 Approach: 'esok already landed, on the mcp compose service, REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID=9f1c8e42-... (the cert principal) and REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY=/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key (the materialized Ed25519 key, fetched from SSM /rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key by infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh to the bind-mount the container reads).'

fd4a Scope enumerates the mcp compose env: REBAR_MCP_TRANSPORT, REBAR_MCP_HTTP_HOST/PORT, REBAR_MCP_HTTP_TLS_AT_EDGE, REBAR_MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS/ORIGINS, REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ENABLED, REBAR_MCP_AUTH_STRATEGIES, REBAR_MCP_AUTH_RESOURCE_SERVER_URL, REBAR_MCP_AUTH_STATIC_TOKENS_FILE — no REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID, no REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY, no opcert-ed25519-key mount.
9015 (avians) Transform materializes only MCP_CLIENT_PAT_{COPILOT,CODEX,CLAUDE} and mcp-static-tokens.json; it does not fetch/materialize the opcert-ed25519-key or set REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID.
b173 depends only on mosasaur (ADR) — not on esok/avians — so the child b173 body treats the env provisioning as an already-satisfied precondition owned elsewhere, but no sibling AC delivers it.
findings.finding: The opcert signing provisioning on the mcp compose service (REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID=9f1c8e42-... and REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY plus the opcert-ed25519-key secret mount/fetch) is owned by NO child's stated scope: b173 (goose) asserts esok already landed it, but fd4a (esok) does not include those env vars/secret in its compose scope, and 9015 (avians) materializes only MCP_CLIENT_PAT_* from SSM, not the opcert key.
scenarios: b173 AC1 (move-1 signing round-trip): the container's signing path cannot compose the signer binding because REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID / cfg.identity.signing_key are not set on the mcp service, so certs sign with the wrong key (the exact failure b173 warns about) — but no sibling provisions them.

At deploy: the mcp container boots without an opcert env_id/key, so MCP-minted plan-review/completion certs never verify against the pinned pubkey, defeating parent AC4's 'the MCP container signs under the box's existing opcert env'.
findings.suggested_fix: Either extend fd4a's compose scope to set REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID + REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY and the opcert-key mount and extend 9015 to materialize opcert-ed25519-key, or move that provisioning into b173's scope; then make b173 depend on esok+avians. Correct b173's Approach text which currently asserts esok 'already landed' those vars.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a 9015 AC oracle asserting the per-client PAT SSM param is defined in infra/terraform/ssm.tf's rebar_secret_params set (grep/terraform-parse), so parent AC4's 'as-code in ssm.tf' clause is gated.
evidence: Parent AC4 headline: 'Per-client bearer PATs are SSM-materialized (as-code in ssm.tf) + gitignored (avians)'.
Parent decomposition item 4: 'the SSM parameter is added to the terraform-managed rebar_secret_params set in ssm.tf — reproducible/teardownable as-code'.

9015 Approach lists 'Terraform SSM params for the per-client PATs ... under the existing /rebar/prod/ prefix' but its four AC oracles assert only: git check-ignore guard, fetch-secrets materialization, StaticBearerVerifier contrast, and the runbook — none asserts the ssm.tf/rebar_secret_params terraform edit.
findings.finding: Parent AC4's clause 'Per-client bearer PATs are SSM-materialized (as-code in ssm.tf)' is only partially covered by 9015: the terraform-as-code addition of the SSM param to ssm.tf's rebar_secret_params set (named in parent decomposition item 4) is declared in 9015's Approach but is not asserted by any of 9015's AC oracles (guard/materialize/verifier/runbook), and the parent's own 'Checked' clause verifies only the guard test — the as-code/ssm.tf assertion has no oracle in any sibling.
scenarios: A verifier checking 'as-code in ssm.tf' finds no oracle: the SSM param could be created out-of-band and every 9015 AC would still pass, so the parent's reproducible/teardownable-as-code intent is unverified.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to 9015 an acceptance oracle that structurally asserts the new SSM parameter is a member of the terraform-managed rebar_secret_params set in ssm.tf (mirroring the parent decomposition wording).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the actual per-client config-key citations (doc URL + version/date for Copilot `headers`, Codex `bearer_token_env_var`, Claude `.mcp.json` `headers`/`--header`) in ADR 0104 (or a named research note the ADR links), so the plan's 'citations recorded in the ADR' claim is substantiated.
evidence: Plan: 'Copilot (~/.copilot/mcp-config.json headers) and Codex (~/.codex/config.toml bearer_token_env_var / http_headers) static-bearer-over-HTTP are verified against those tools' current official docs (research 2026-08-24; citations recorded in the ADR).'

ADR 0104 §Decision 1 only states: 'Research confirmed that all three target clients support a static Authorization: Bearer header for a remote HTTP MCP server' — no URLs, doc versions, or per-key citations are present in the ADR text.

The exact config keys are the flag-level failure surface (T3 EMPIRICISM axis a): Codex `bearer_token_env_var`, Copilot `headers` map, Claude `.mcp.json` `headers` — a wrong key name fails silently at connect time.
Evidence class: Unverified — the vendor client docs cannot be probed from this review (resolve_symbol cannot see external CLIs), and the plan's cited evidence trail (ADR citations) is absent.
findings.finding: The plan asserts the Copilot/Codex/Claude static-bearer config-key shapes are 'verified against those tools' current official docs (research 2026-08-24; citations recorded in the ADR),' but ADR 0104 records no such citations — only a general 'Research confirmed … support a static Authorization: Bearer header' statement with no doc URL/version for the specific config-file keys or paths.
findings.location: Plan summary, Exposure/auth bullet ('verified against those tools' current official docs … citations recorded in the ADR'); ADR docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md §Decision 1
scenarios: A reviewer or operator tries to confirm the Codex `bearer_token_env_var` / Copilot `headers` keys against the recorded research and finds no citation in the ADR to check against.
A future client-doc change silently invalidates a key with no dated citation to diff against.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to ADR 0104 §Decision 1 a short citations block listing, per client, the observed official-doc URL and the date/version confirming the exact config-file key and path used (Copilot mcp-config.json `headers`; Codex config.toml `[mcp_servers.rebar]` `bearer_token_env_var`; Claude .mcp.json `headers` / `--header`).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make explicit (in the olm slice and AC-4) that the vendor-CLI key confirmation is skip-gated in CI and that the authoritative per-client-key proof is the operator-run jackal live smoke — or pin the CLIs into the test environment so the client-binary tier actually runs.
evidence: The three client-binary acceptance tests are guarded by `@pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which('copilot'/'codex'/'claude') is None, reason='… CLI not installed')`.

The always-run tests exercise a loopback rebar-mcp with the RESOLVED bearer via a hand-rolled `_expand_env` / `bearer_token_env_var` loader in the TEST — they confirm rebar's server accepts the token, not that each vendor CLI actually reads that config key and emits the header.
Auth/HTTPS preconditions are otherwise well stated (loopback bind, http_tls_at_edge, allowlists, static digests) — this finding is only about the client-side key surface.
findings.finding: The automated confirmation of the three client config-key shapes is skip-gated on the CLI being installed (`@pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which(...) is None)`), so in CI without copilot/codex/claude present the config-key surface is not empirically exercised — the only live proof is the deferred operator-run jackal smoke.
findings.location: olm slice / AC-4 ('each client lists the rebar server and runs a basic read tool'); tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py (test_copilot_cli_loads_committed_config / test_codex_cli_loads_committed_config / test_claude_cli_loads_committed_config)
scenarios: CI runs olm's config test on a runner without the three CLIs; the client-binary tests skip, the always-run tests pass against a test-local loader, and a wrong vendor key ships undetected until the operator smoke.
